correctness.rationale: Finite-field Fourier inversion of the complete s-line measurements recovers all fiber sums of \(t^2-ct\). Their exact involution kernels are intersected by composing reflections into translations by H_C. The odd-order quotient has one fixed orbit and (q/h−1)/2 swapped pairs, giving the exact nullity and explicit basis. The basis establishes the support minimum \(2h\), and the standard difference-of-two-sparse-vectors argument gives a necessary-and-sufficient sparse threshold. Complete recovery iff affine slopes span F_q, requiring at least \(m+1\) views. Exact rational matrix tests for 390 offset configurations and separately implemented numerical Fourier rank tests passed, with a sharp six-support F9 case; finite checks supplement the proof.
